title: Beef Stroganoff
subtitle: Silky sauce, wide noodles
description: Silky sauce, wide noodles. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

ingredients.name: Beef sirloin or chuck, sliced thin

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Beef Stroganoff in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Use Cremini mushrooms, sliced, Yellow onion, sliced, Fresh parsley, chopped as listed — measure each before heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch beef. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Slice beef and prep mushrooms
steps.instruction: Slice beef across the grain into thin strips. Pat dry and season with salt, pepper, and paprika. Slice mushrooms and onion — uniform pieces cook evenly in one pan.

steps.title: Sear beef in batches
steps.instruction: Melt 2 tbsp butter in a large skillet over high heat. Sear beef in a single layer 2 minutes per side until browned but still pink inside. Transfer to a plate — do not crowd or you steam instead of sear. Target 145°F for steaks, 160°F for ground at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Cook mushrooms and onions
steps.instruction: Add remaining butter to the pan. Cook mushrooms and onions over medium heat 10–12 minutes until deeply browned and moisture evaporates. Stir in garlic 30 seconds until fragrant.

steps.title: Build the stroganoff sauce
steps.instruction: Sprinkle flour over vegetables; cook 1 minute. Whisk in beef broth and Worcestershire; simmer 5 minutes until thickened. Remove from heat, stir in Dijon, then fold in sour cream — boiling curdles sour cream. Target 145°F for steaks, 160°F for ground at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Return beef and simmer gently
steps.instruction: Return beef and any juices to the pan. Simmer 5–8 minutes on low until beef is tender and sauce coats a spoon. Taste for salt — beef broth varies. Target 145°F for steaks, 160°F for ground at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Beef Stroganoff onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Boil noodles and serve
steps.instruction: Boil egg noodles in salted water until tender; drain well. Toss noodles with stroganoff on sheet trays or serve noodles first with sauce ladled over. Finish with parsley.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Serve wide egg noodles with stroganoff sauce ladled over — sour cream sauce stays separate from any tomato pan.
Keep extra parsley and black pepper at the line; mushrooms should be visible in every scoop.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Add a splash of stock or water when reheating — thick sauces tighten in the fridge.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Silky sauce, wide noodles. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Any short pasta shape works — penne, rigatoni, or spaghetti.
mealPrepNotes: Prep mise en place before the shift — Beef Stroganoff runs smoother when proteins are trimmed, spices are pre-measured, and hotel pans are labeled before the first tone.
